1.why: All seven screens are static, uncluttered cards with no pop-ups, animations, or moving images.

2.why: Primary actions use solid blue buttons with bold step headings and a highlighted progress chip, though the large dark logs panel also draws significant attention.

3.why: Each screen presents one clearly labeled task, but retrieving the recovery code requires reading a technical logs panel and the instruction even references the 'browser console'.

4.why: Rules and the four-step progress indicator remain visible on screen, yet the user must transcribe a 30-character code and create a 12+ character password meeting four character classes.

5.why: No password manager, autofill, or 'remember me' option appears on any of the seven screens.

6.why: The persistent logs panel re-displays her completed actions for recognition, but there are no saved credentials or other familiar stored items shown.

7.why: Instruction text is short and mostly plain, but jargon such as 'browser console', 'mock', and 'simulate' appears in user-facing copy.

8.why: No error message is shown in any screenshot, so whether errors describe the problem and fix cannot be confirmed.

9.why: The logs panel displays the exact code to enter ('use this code here: ...'), but input fields have no placeholder examples and no sample password is provided.

10.why: The choices actually offered (reset vs. sign in; verify code, simulated link, or new code) are clearly labeled, though no face-login option exists.

11.why: Screens present at most two to three options, and most steps require only a single action.

12.why: Green banners and log lines confirm outcomes ('You are securely signed in', 'Request confirmed'), but some results, such as the password being saved, are only implied by advancing or recorded in the technical logs.

13.why: Every step opens with a short guiding tip, and each page includes a 'Help and safety' section plus a footer help note.

14.why: A visible 'Request a new code' button and the stated absence of countdowns support retrying, although wrong-entry error handling is never demonstrated.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the same header, progress chips, card layout, button styles, logs panel, and footer, keeping the design highly consistent.
